lines.text: 'Twas a great blessing to behold my sister one final time.
Let not haste overcome thee. One drink, and thy trouble shall seem no great matter.
I dream'd a dream much too sumptuous for one of my estate. I shall never forget it.
Thy face appears to shine. Doth our reunion after this long while bring thee joy?
Many things have I cleaved in my days, but never would I wish to sever the bond betwixt us.
To behold my comrades thus restored doth awaken within me new feeling.
Hath thy business taken thee elsewhere? Thou art aloof as a passing shadow.
Folly followeth haste. I shall prepare us some fine liquor; return in thine own good time.
Knowest thou where to find good, strong drink? Lead me thither.
Pray, what manner of splendidly adorned edifice stands yonder?
Much bettered is this place since my previous visitation. The fruit, no doubt, of thine endeavors.
I shall honor my sister's wish and live in happiness. Pray, accompany me, my Lord.
This gift of thine doth truly amaze. My body is grown lighter.
Methinks I could cleave aught asunder.
It now seems to me our triumph on the surface is nigh.
Bestowest thou on me such a precious gift?
I fear this may inspire jealousy in the others.
When all is done, I shall repay this grace with a most exquisite bottle of liquor.
I see thou desirest to drink with me. Thy countenance tells all.
I marvel how thou utterest such indiscretions with facility, my Lord.
Thy presence makes me drunk without liquor, as it were.
Shall I go forth?
Didst thou call?
I shall lead.
Let us give them battle.
Hold thy distance and observe, my Lord.
Good fortune. My body and blade are restless.
Be not troubled. I shall end this swiftly.
There is no need to rush.
I am sheathing my blade.
There is virtue in rest.
The time has come.
Bloom. Beyond the fade.
Grant them no respite.
An easy foe.
Cleaved in twain.
Farewell.
Ngh!
Ugh!
How vexing.
Is my blade... grown dull...?
Are thou watching, Rose? Behold thy sister, whom thou lovest so.
